# The Yantra App (`yantra ui`)

`yantra ui` opens Yantra in its own browser window. The window has no address
bar. It is served by a small **app host** process that runs on your computer
and listens only on `127.0.0.1`. You do not need a terminal open to keep using
the window. No other web page or local program can drive it. The app page
loads nothing from anywhere except the host.

The host is a supervisor, not an executor. Every run or change the app starts
runs as an ordinary Yantra command, in its own background process. That process
uses the same handler and arguments a terminal would. Each command starts at
most once. A run keeps going and keeps its data if the window, the host or
both go away.

The window has a top bar with the Yantra status mark and links to **Home** and
the **Ledger**, plus a connection banner. Its run screens are the **Ledger**
(every run), the **Run result** of one run, its **Audit**, and bounded
**file viewers**. These screens only read: they show any run Yantra recorded,
whether it came from the terminal, the scheduler daemon or the app. The queue,
run-following and attendance behavior described below belongs to the host.

## What It Does

### Opens one app host per data directory

- `yantra ui` looks for a running app host for the current data directory. If
  one is running and ready, it is reused. Otherwise `yantra ui` starts one in
  the background and waits up to 10 seconds for it to become ready.
- Two `yantra ui` commands started at the same moment still end up with one
  host. The second one reuses the first one's host.
- `yantra ui` asks the host for a **launch code** and builds the URL
  `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/#code=<code>`. A launch code works once, for 60
  seconds. The port is chosen fresh each time a host starts.
- The window removes the code from its address before it does anything else.
  It then exchanges the code for a session (see
  [Privacy and security](#privacy-and-security)).
- If the running host is from a different Yantra version than the CLI you ran,
  `yantra ui` still reuses it. It prints this note on stderr:
  ``The running app is Yantra <old>; close the app and run `yantra ui` to use <new>.``
  The note is not printed with `--json`.

### Chooses the browser that opens the window

`yantra ui` opens the first browser it finds, in this order:

1. **Google Chrome** installed on the system, from the stable, beta, dev or
   canary channel. Chrome for Testing is never used at this step.
2. **Microsoft Edge**, at its standard install locations:
   - Windows: `Microsoft\Edge\Application\msedge.exe` under
     `Program Files (x86)`, then under `Program Files`.
   - macOS: `/Applications/Microsoft Edge.app`.
   - Linux: `microsoft-edge` or `microsoft-edge-stable` on `PATH`.
3. **The browser Yantra uses for its own runs**, as `yantra browser` resolves
   it.

Whichever browser is chosen gets the same arguments: `--app=<url>`,
`--user-data-dir=<data-dir>/ui/chrome-profile`, `--no-first-run` and
`--no-default-browser-check`. The window therefore uses its own profile,
separate from your everyday browsing profile and from every automation
profile. It never gets a remote-debugging or automation flag. The browser is
started in the background, and `yantra ui` exits without waiting for it.

If no browser is found, `yantra ui` still prints the URL so that you can open
it yourself, and exits with code 3:

```text
http://127.0.0.1:53817/#code=…
No Chrome, Edge or Yantra browser was found to open the app. Run `yantra browser install`, or open the URL above in Chrome or Edge.
```

### Shows its connection state

A banner under the top bar reports the window's connection to the host. It is
a polite live region, so screen readers announce changes without moving focus.

| State         | What the window shows                                                                                                                                    |
| ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Connecting    | `Connecting to Yantra…`                                                                                                                                  |
| Connected     | No banner. The Home page reads `Connected to the Yantra on this computer.`                                                                               |
| Disconnected  | `Disconnected from Yantra. Reconnecting in <n> s.` (or `Reconnecting…`). Retries back off from 0.5 to 10 seconds, with jitter.                           |
| Session ended | ``Session ended — run `yantra ui` to reopen.`` The page is replaced by **Session ended**: "Run `yantra ui` to reopen the Yantra app."                    |
| Incompatible  | ``This window cannot talk to Yantra <version>. Run `yantra ui` to reopen.`` The page shows **Session ended** with "The running app is Yantra <version>." |

A window's session ends, and the window stops trying to reconnect, when:

- it has been unable to reconnect for 5 minutes;
- the host refuses its credentials, for example because the session expired;
- it was opened 12 hours ago, whether or not it is connected; or
- it was loaded without a usable code, for example a launch URL opened a
  second time or more than 60 seconds after `yantra ui` printed it.

Once a session has ended, only `yantra ui` opens a new window.

**Reloading.** While a window is connected, it fetches a fresh **resume code**
every 45 seconds and keeps it in that tab's `sessionStorage`. A resume code is
single-use and lasts 60 seconds. Pressing F5 exchanges it for a new session for
the same window, and the old session is revoked at that moment. If the tab
cannot use `sessionStorage`, a reload ends the session.

**New app build.** If the page and the host come from different app builds,
the page reloads itself into the host's build. It waits until it is idle:
no request in flight and no text field focused.

### Applies the app appearance preferences

| Preference    | Values                    | Default  | Effect                                                         |
| ------------- | ------------------------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ui.theme`    | `system`, `light`, `dark` | `system` | Follow the operating system's light/dark setting, or force one |
| `ui.surfaces` | `glass`, `solid`          | `glass`  | Translucent glass surfaces, or solid surfaces                  |

The window reads the effective values from the same view as
`yantra profile --json`, so a value left at its default or set by hand in
`profile.yaml` also applies. Any unrecognized value falls back to the default.

The window applies the preferences each time it connects. It also applies them
again shortly after `profile.yaml` changes (the host checks every 2 seconds).
`yantra prefs set` stores its value in the preference index, not in
`profile.yaml`, so an open window picks that change up the next time it
connects. Reload the window to apply it at once.

### Shows CLI, daemon and app runs without a reload

While a window is subscribed, the host watches the runs directory and the
history index every 2 seconds. File-system change hints, where available,
trigger an earlier check. Changes are batched for a quarter of a second, then
the host tells the window which runs changed and which runs currently hold a
live lease.

This applies to runs from any source: the terminal, the scheduler daemon or
the app. If file watching is unavailable, the host falls back to polling alone
and logs that once.

### Lists every run in the Ledger

The **Ledger** (`/runs`, **Ledger** in the top bar) lists every run Yantra has
recorded. It reads runs through the same function as `yantra list`, after the
same reconciliation, so a run's words match what `yantra list` prints.

- **Active** lists runs that have not ended. It is never paged. Each run shows
  its displayed state instead of an outcome: `queued`, `starting`, `running`,
  `waiting for you`, `needs review`, `start outcome unknown` or
  `worker not responding`. A run whose manifest says it is running but whose
  owner cannot be verified reads `status unknown`, never `running`. The region
  reads "No runs in progress." when it is empty.
- **History** is a table of runs that ended, newest first, with the columns
  Outcome, Title, Mode, Started, Duration, Cost and Run ID. It loads 50 runs at
  a time as you scroll. Selecting a row opens its Run result.
- **The Outcome column** prints the same words as `yantra list`: the status,
  then the outcome when one was recorded (for example `succeeded fulfilled`).
  `interrupted` appears as a separate chip. Each outcome also has an icon, so
  color is never the only signal. A value a run did not record shows `—`.

**Filters.** You can narrow History by:

| Filter  | Choices                                                                                                |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Outcome | Any of `fulfilled`, `partial`, `handoff`, `failed`, `aborted` and **no outcome recorded** (older runs) |
| Mode    | **Any mode**, or one of `ask`, `research`, `do`, `run`                                                 |
| From/To | Calendar days, inclusive, in your time zone                                                            |
| Search  | Text found in the run's goal or workflow name, or in its run ID (any case, at most 200 characters)     |

The filters are kept in the page's URL as `outcome` (comma-separated), `mode`,
`since`, `until` and `q`. They are written a quarter of a second after you
stop changing them. Reloading the window, or going back and forward, keeps
them. An unrecognized value is dropped rather than shown as an error. With
filters set and no match, History reads "No runs match these filters."

**Live updates.** When runs change, the Ledger refreshes its first page and
merges it into what you have already loaded, so no loaded row is lost. New
runs are announced to screen readers as, for example, "2 new runs". Focus
never moves.

**Reading from files.** If the history index is unavailable, the Ledger reads
run directories instead and says: "History index unavailable — showing runs
from files only. Run `yantra doctor` to rebuild the index." Each page then
reads at most 2,000 run directories. When it stops there, the Ledger says
"Showing the newest runs; refine filters to search further."

### Shows each run's result

Selecting a run opens its **Run result** (`/runs/<run-id>`), the app's form of
`yantra open <run-id>`. The header shows:

- the title: the Brief's or document's title, else the run's goal, else the
  workflow name, else the run ID;
- the outcome badge, as in the Ledger, or the live state of a run that has not
  ended;
- the mode, start and end times, and duration;
- the run ID, and its terminal twin `yantra open <run-id>` labelled
  **In a terminal**, with a copy button.

A run whose manifest says it is running but whose owner cannot be verified
also shows "Status unknown — the owner of this run can’t be verified." A run
that is still going refreshes when it changes.

The page has three tabs: **Result**, **Audit** and **Files**.

**What the page reads.** Everything comes from the run's directory, and each
file is read on its own:

| File                                            | Used for                                                                                              |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `manifest.json`                                 | Mode, title, times, status, outcome, how the run stopped and whether it was interrupted               |
| `brief.json`, else `document.json`              | The Brief or templated document. With neither, the Result tab shows the no-document result            |
| `outputs.json`                                  | A workflow run's outputs                                                                              |
| `run-health.json`                               | The run health counts                                                                                 |
| `report.md`                                     | Loaded only when shown                                                                                |
| `run-events.jsonl`, `events.jsonl`, `report.md` | Why the run ended, when the manifest does not say (see [Runs without a Brief](#runs-without-a-brief)) |
| The lease                                       | Whether a run that has not ended is still owned                                                       |
| Every other file                                | The **Files** list, limited to files the app may show                                                 |

**One bad file never breaks the page.** Each of the document, outputs and run
health has its own state:

| State        | What the page shows                                                                                         |
| ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Missing      | `No <thing> recorded for this run.`                                                                         |
| Corrupt      | `The <thing> (<file>) could not be read: <reason>.` The reason is a short summary, never the file's content |
| Older format | `The <thing> (<file>) was written in an older format (<version>) that this app cannot show.`                |
| Too large    | `The <thing> (<file>) is too large to show here: <size>, over the <limit> limit.` plus **Show in folder**   |

When a Brief or document is corrupt or in an older format, the page also
offers **Open brief.md** (or `document.md`) in the Markdown viewer and
**Download brief.html** (or `document.html`), when the run has those files.
A corrupt `manifest.json` still gives a page: the mode reads `unknown` and the
title is the run ID.

Only an unknown run replaces the whole page: it shows **Run not found** with a
link back to the Ledger. If the run cannot be loaded for another reason, the
page shows **Couldn’t load this run** with the reason and **Retry**.

### Renders Briefs and templated documents

On the **Result** tab, a Brief appears in the same order the terminal and HTML
renderers use:

1. condition statuses, with each status word as recorded (`verified`,
   `unverified`, `violated`);
2. **Overview**;
3. **Key findings**, with one level of child findings. Editorial findings are
   marked `editorial` only when some findings are not editorial;
4. each section, with `alternatives` sections labelled;
5. **Comparison**, a table with an Evidence column of citation chips per row;
6. **Requirements** (do runs), with `met`, `unmet` or `not_applicable`, the
   reason, any exemptions and "+N more";
7. **Captures**, grouped into capture sets, each marked `complete` or
   `incomplete` and with any `clipped_width`, `truncated` or `beyond_viewport`
   label;
8. **Sources** (cited) and **Also consulted** (fetched but not cited), each
   with its number, host and a link;
9. **Notices**, grouped by kind, or "No notices recorded.";
10. a footer with the synthesis mode, search provider, coverage, citation
    check, usage and whether a deterministic fallback was used.

A **templated document** shows "From template `<name>`", its rendered
Markdown, then Sources, Also consulted, Notices and the same footer.

**Untrusted text stays inert.** The overview, findings, sections, templated
documents and `report.md` render through a Markdown renderer that skips raw
HTML; all other text is shown escaped. Only `http` and `https` links become
links, and they open in a new tab with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`. An image
in Markdown is never loaded; its alt text is shown instead. Captures load only
through the host's signed URLs.

### Opens citation evidence in one click

Every source citation `[n]` and every action citation `A<n>` in a Brief is a
button. Its tooltip previews the host and title, or the action kind and label.
Pressing it opens the **Evidence** pane beside the document and moves focus to
the pane's heading. The pane shows one item at a time. Escape or **Close**
returns focus to the chip you pressed.

- **A source** (`Source 3`) shows its title, host, URL, final URL when it
  differs, fetch and publish times, and whether it was cited or only
  consulted. Its quote is the excerpt the run recorded for that source, or
  "Quote not recorded for this run".
- **An action** (`Action A2`) shows the action kind, its label with where the
  label came from and the engine's confidence, the form section, and the
  target's host, element ref, page epoch and tool call. Its verification is
  shown as recorded. A refused submit shows why. **Show capture** opens the
  matching capture in the gallery.
- **A protected fill** (a password, autocomplete-protected or secret-marked
  field, or a stored secret) shows a fixed mask, `••••••••`, with
  "Protected — <reason>" and the readback verdict. The mask is the same for
  every value, so it reveals neither the value nor its length.
- **Cited by** lists every finding, section, comparison row and condition that
  cites the item. Each entry scrolls to that claim and focuses it.

A `[n]` that names no source of the Brief stays plain text. An `A<n>` that the
run did not record, and every `A<n>` in an older Brief without action
evidence, opens "Action evidence not recorded for this run". In a templated
document, only source citations are chips.

### Runs without a Brief

A run that saved no Brief or document still gets a complete Result tab. This
covers a workflow without synthesis, a run that failed before its Brief, and
interrupted or older runs. Every region shows a value or says plainly that
nothing was recorded:

1. **Outcome**: the outcome badge and how the run stopped. An interrupted run
   adds "The run’s owner stopped before it finished." followed by "The outcome
   follows the evidence it left: `<outcome>`." (or "No outcome was
   recorded.").
2. **Why it ended**: the failure class, message, blocker, safest next action
   and termination reason, as recorded. A line names where the reason was
   found: the run-event stream (`run-events.jsonl`), `manifest.json`,
   `events.jsonl` or `report.md`, tried in that order. Text is cut at 500
   characters.
3. **Outputs**: a workflow run's outputs in the JSON viewer, "The workflow
   declared no outputs.", or the outputs' state.
4. **Run health**: the counts in the same words as the `## Run Health` section
   of `report.md`, or "No run health was recorded for this run."
5. **Notices**: how many notices run health counted, pointing to `report.md`,
   or "No notices recorded."
6. **report.md**: the report, rendered safely. Over 512 KiB, only the first
   512 KiB is shown, cut at the end of a line, under "Showing the first part
   of report.md; the whole file is `<size>`." with **Show in folder**.
7. **Files**: the run's file list, as on the Files tab.

### Files and viewers

The **Files** tab lists every file of the run the app may show, with its size
and an action:

- **View** opens the file in its viewer (`/runs/<run-id>/artifacts/<path>`).
- **Download** saves an HTML file (`brief.html`, `document.html`). HTML is
  never opened in the app.
- `brief.json` and `document.json` read "Shown on the Result tab".

Files the app never serves are not listed at all (see
[Privacy and security](#privacy-and-security)). The list walks the run
directory and its direct subdirectories, and stops at 2,000 files with "Only
the first 2,000 files are listed."

| Viewer   | Files                                                                                                                                                                                   | How it reads                                                                                                                                                      |
| -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| JSONL    | `events.jsonl`, `run-events.jsonl`, `runtime.jsonl`, `tool-calls.jsonl`, `confirmations.jsonl`, `secrets.jsonl` (key names only), `interventions.jsonl`, `agent.jsonl`, `agent/*.jsonl` | Any length, in windows of 200 lines as you scroll                                                                                                                 |
| JSON     | `outputs.json`, `manifest.json`, `usage.json`, `run-health.json`, `contract.json`, `trace.json`, `schedule.json`, `execution-receipt.json`                                              | A collapsible tree. Strings over 2 KiB are folded behind **Show all**; at most 500 entries per level. A file that is not valid JSON is shown as text, with a note |
| Markdown | `report.md`, `brief.md`, `document.md`                                                                                                                                                  | Rendered safely, as on the Result tab                                                                                                                             |
| Text     | `captures/cap-*.txt`                                                                                                                                                                    | Plain, escaped text                                                                                                                                               |
| Image    | `screenshots/*.png`, `captures/*.png`                                                                                                                                                   | Fitted to the page, or at **Natural size**                                                                                                                        |

**The JSONL viewer:**

- The list shows `<n> lines`, or `At least <n> lines` until the whole file has
  been counted. Scrolling further, or **Go to the end**, counts the rest.
  **Go to the end** also opens the last line.
- A line of `events.jsonl` or `run-events.jsonl` with a known event kind shows
  a one-line summary, such as `step completed · <step id>`.
- Selecting a line shows it in full in an inspector beside the list, with
  `kind`, `seq` and `ts` first. The inspector shows at most 6 levels and 200
  entries per level, then "+N more".
- A line that is not valid JSON shows as raw text with a `not valid JSON` chip.
  Only that line is affected.
- A line over 16 KiB is cut and marked `cut at 16 KiB`; its detail says how
  much more is in the file.
- A last line that is still being written is never shown. The viewer says
  "The last line is still being written."

**Show in folder.** Wherever a file is too large to show, the page offers
**Show in folder**. In this release it always appears as a terminal twin: the
label **Show in folder**, the command `yantra open <run-id> --artifact dir` and
a copy button. Run that command in a terminal to open the run's directory. The
app does not run it for you yet.

### Audits a run

The **Audit** tab (also `/runs/<run-id>/audit`) tells the same story as
`yantra audit <run-id>`, from the same builder, with tool calls and captures
loaded 500 rows at a time. Secret lookups show key names only. See
[Diagnostics and Audit](diagnostics-and-audit.md) for what it contains.

### Older runs and size limits

**Older runs.** Runs from earlier Yantra versions open without errors:

- a run with only `manifest.json` and `report.md` gets the no-document result;
- a run with no outcome shows its status word alone, and the Ledger's **no
  outcome recorded** filter finds it;
- a Brief from an older format shows the older-format state, with `brief.md`
  and `brief.html` as fallbacks;
- a Brief without action evidence opens "Action evidence not recorded for this
  run" for each `A<n>`;
- a run with no `run-health.json` says "No run health was recorded for this
  run.";
- an interrupted run without a run-event stream still shows the interrupted
  wording, with the reason from its manifest, events or report.

**Size limits.** Nothing the app shows is read without a limit. Over a limit,
you see this instead:

| What                                                | Limit                      | Over the limit                                                                                                      |
| --------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `brief.json`, `document.json`                       | 512 KiB                    | The too-large state, with **Show in folder**                                                                        |
| `outputs.json` on the Result tab                    | 256 KiB                    | The too-large state, with **Show in folder**                                                                        |
| The whole Run result                                | 768 KiB                    | The document, then the outputs, show the too-large state; as a last resort the file list stops at 200 files         |
| `report.md` on the Result tab                       | 512 KiB                    | The first 512 KiB, cut at a line, with a banner and **Show in folder**                                              |
| `report.md` in the viewer                           | 512 KiB                    | `report.md is too large to open here (<size>).` with **Show in folder**                                             |
| `brief.md`, `document.md`, JSON files, capture text | 2 MiB                      | `<file> is too large to open here (<size>).` with **Show in folder**                                                |
| Images                                              | 20 MiB                     | `<file> is too large to show here (<size>).` with **Show in folder**; in the capture gallery, a placeholder instead |
| JSONL files                                         | None for the file          | Read in 200-line windows; each line cut at 16 KiB                                                                   |
| Ledger pages                                        | 50 runs                    | The next page loads as you scroll                                                                                   |
| Ledger file fallback                                | 2,000 run directories/page | "Showing the newest runs; refine filters to search further."                                                        |
| Audit tool calls and captures                       | 500 rows                   | The next 500 load as you scroll                                                                                     |

A file over its viewer limit is never loaded into the page.

### Runs app-started commands as background workers

When the app starts a command, the host does the following:

1. It checks the command line against the same command registry the terminal
   uses.
2. It records the request under `<data-dir>/ui/invocations/`, keyed by an ID
   the window chose.
3. It starts the command, when the queue allows, as a detached `yantra` worker
   process with the host's environment and the request's working directory.

The worker runs exactly what `yantra <command> …` would run in a terminal. A
run started from the app therefore has the usual run directory, lease, run
socket, `run-events.jsonl` and report, and appears in `yantra list` like any
other run.

**Each request starts at most once.** The worker claims its record before it
does anything else. If the window sends the same request ID again, for example
after a lost reply, the host returns the request's current state and never
starts a second worker.

**Some commands never run from the app queue.** The host refuses them and says
where to go instead:

| Kind of command                                                                                  | What the host says                                                       |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Reads (`list`, `show`, `audit`, `report`, `prefs list`/`get`, `profile`, …)                      | It is a read; the host answers it directly instead of starting a worker. |
| Commands that handle a secret (`secret set`, `secret list`, `secret rm`)                         | It handles a secret and never runs from the app queue.                   |
| Commands that need an app adapter (such as `init`, `config edit`, `open`, `daemon start`/`stop`) | No adapter is registered yet; run it in a terminal.                      |
| Terminal-only commands (`ui`, `config data-dir`)                                                 | Run `yantra <command>` in a terminal.                                    |

### Queues runs, two at a time

- **Runs** (`ask`, `research`, `do`, `run`, `resume` and other run commands)
  take a slot. At most **two** run at once.
- **Exclusive** commands, such as `browser install` and `browser update`, run
  only when no run is active. While one is active, no new run starts.
- **Commands that only change something** (mutating commands) take no slot and
  start right away.
- Waiting items start strictly in arrival order. An item starts only when it is
  first in line and its slot is free.
- The queue is kept on disk. It survives the window closing and the host
  restarting.

### Asks for review when something changed while queued

When the app submits a command, it records the effective settings and the
workflow or template file contents it showed you. Just before a queued item
starts, the host works those settings out again, without running anything. It
uses the same precedence the worker will use, and re-hashes the files.

If anything differs, the item moves to **needs review** and lists each
difference, with the value you submitted and the current value. A value that
came from an environment variable is shown only by the variable's name, such
as `$YANTRA_AGENT_MODEL`, never by its value. A workflow file that no longer
exists also counts as a difference.

You then choose one of:

- **Use the current values:** the item goes back in the queue as it is.
- **Use the submitted values:** each differing value is added as an explicit
  flag of the command. This choice is unavailable if a workflow or template file
  changed, or if any difference cannot be expressed as a flag of that command.
- **Discard** the item.

### Stops and restarts items

- **Stopping an item that has not started** withdraws it. If a worker was being
  started at that moment, its claim is refused and it exits without doing
  anything.
- **Stopping a started item** asks its run to cancel through the run's socket.
  If the process is still alive after 10 seconds, the host ends that exact
  process tree, identified by creation identity rather than by a bare process
  ID. The run is then reconciled, so it records an outcome.
- **A command with no run** gets the same 10 seconds, and is then ended by
  identity.
- **An item that never started** can be started again at once. Its worker
  provably never ran.
- **An item whose start is unknown** (starting the worker failed partway, so it
  may or may not have run) starts again only after you confirm. The host warns:
  "The earlier start of this item is unknown: it may already have run, so
  starting it again may repeat its effects."

### Survives a window, host or worker going away

| What goes away | What happens                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The window     | Runs and the queue continue. The window's session stays valid for 5 minutes after its last connection closes.                                                                                                                                              |
| The host       | Workers keep running. The host never signals a worker when it stops. An open window shows **Disconnected** and cannot reconnect to a new host. Run `yantra ui` again. It starts a new host, which first recovers every request and then resumes the queue. |
| A worker       | Yantra's usual run reconciliation, which also runs when a host starts, ends its run with an `owner_lost` outcome (`partial` or `failed`, from its evidence). The next host start finishes the request with the reason `owner_lost`.                        |

**Recovery on host start** handles each request by its state:

- A request that had not been claimed by its worker becomes **never started**.
  A worker that tries to claim it later is refused.
- A worker that is still alive is left alone. The new host attaches to its run
  as soon as a window follows that run. The window can ask for events from the
  last sequence number it saw, and receives every later event exactly once:
  first from `run-events.jsonl`, then live.
- A worker that has died has its run reconciled, and the request is finished
  as `owner_lost`.
- A worker whose liveness cannot be verified is left unchanged. It is never
  treated as dead.

Queued items are not started by recovery. They start only through the normal
queue, which still runs drift review and the slot check for each one.

**Run following.** If a run's worker speaks an older run-channel version, the
window is told that live updates are unavailable for that run, and the worker
is never stopped. A worker that sends nothing for 30 seconds is reported as not
responding.

**Idle exit.** The host shuts itself down after 10 minutes during which no
window is connected and nothing is queued or starting. Running workers neither
keep it alive nor are touched when it exits. Any window connection or new
request cancels the countdown.

### Counts who is watching (attendance)

A window counts as **attending** only if all three of these hold:

- it is connected;
- it has asked to receive interventions;
- it has checked in within the last 30 seconds. The app checks in every 10
  seconds.

The host sends the number of attending windows to every run it is following.
It sends the number when it changes, when it starts following a run, and every
10 seconds.

**With no window, the count is 0.** A long-running host or a full queue never
counts as someone watching. The host logs only changes in the count. What a run
does with the count is the run's own behavior.

Windows that asked for interventions are also sent each followed run's
`intervention_raised` and `intervention_resolved` events.

## How to Use It

```bash
# Open the app (starts the host if needed)
yantra ui

# Print the URL instead of opening a window
yantra ui --print

# Machine-readable result; still opens the window
yantra ui --json

# Both: print the URL as JSON, open nothing
yantra ui --print --json

# Make the app dark with solid surfaces
yantra prefs set ui.theme dark
yantra prefs set ui.surfaces solid
```

With `--print`, open the URL yourself in a browser on the same computer within
60 seconds. Each `yantra ui --print` issues a new single-use code from the same
host.

To set the appearance by hand, edit `profile.yaml`:

```yaml
ui:
  theme: dark
  surfaces: solid
```

`yantra config set ui.theme …` does not write the setting. It redirects you to
`yantra prefs set ui.theme …`. An invalid value, such as
`yantra prefs set ui.surfaces frosted`, exits with code 1 and lists the valid
values. Only these two `ui.*` keys exist.

### Review a run

1. Run `yantra ui` and choose **Ledger** in the top bar.
2. Narrow the list with the Outcome, Mode, From/To and Search filters, for
   example **failed** runs of mode `research` this week.
3. Select a run. Its **Result** tab shows the Brief, document or no-document
   result.
4. Press any `[n]` or `A<n>` chip to see its evidence in the side pane. Press
   Escape to return to the chip.
5. Open **Audit** for secret use, consent, tool calls and model calls, or
   **Files** to open any file the app may show.

The run screens and their in-app paths:

| Screen     | Path                                                                             | Terminal twin                         |
| ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| Ledger     | `/runs?outcome=failed&mode=research&since=2026-11-01&until=2026-11-07&q=invoice` | `yantra list`                         |
| Run result | `/runs/<run-id>`                                                                 | `yantra open <run-id>`                |
| Audit      | `/runs/<run-id>/audit`                                                           | `yantra audit <run-id>`               |
| A file     | `/runs/<run-id>/artifacts/<path>`                                                | `yantra open <run-id> --artifact dir` |

`yantra list` has no flags yet for the Ledger's outcome, mode, date and text
filters.

## Inputs and Outputs

### `yantra ui` options

| Option    | Effect                                                                    |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--print` | Print the app URL instead of opening a window                             |
| `--json`  | Emit JSON describing the opened app (the URL, too, when no browser opens) |

In human mode a successful open prints `Opened the Yantra app in <browser>.`,
for example `Google Chrome` or `Microsoft Edge`. `--print` prints the URL alone.

### `--json` output

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "url": "http://127.0.0.1:53817/#code=…",
  "port": 53817,
  "hostPid": 41236,
  "reused": true
}
```

`reused` is `true` when an already-running host was used. If no browser is
found, the same JSON goes to stdout and the error goes to stderr.

### Exit codes

| Code | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ---- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `0`  | The window opened, or the URL was printed                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `1`  | Invalid usage, such as an unknown option or an extra argument                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `3`  | No browser was found (the URL is still printed); the host lock cannot be verified or read; the host exited before it was ready, or was not ready within 10 seconds (the message names `host.log`); the host could not listen on `127.0.0.1`; the app files are missing ("Rebuild Yantra (pnpm build)."); or the host's control socket was unreachable |

Every exit-3 message ends with one next step. If the host lock is held by a
process whose liveness cannot be verified, the message says:

```text
Close any running Yantra app; if none is running, delete the host.lock file in the data directory's ui folder and run `yantra ui` again.
```

### Host reads behind the run screens

The run screens use these host requests, over the window's authenticated
connection. Each one checks the run ID before it touches the disk. Each
response is bounded so that it stays below the host's 1 MiB message limit.

| Request                                                     | Returns                                                                                                                             |
| ----------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `read.list` (`target: runs`)                                | One Ledger page: `items` in `yantra list --json` form, `next_cursor`, `source` (`index` or `files`), `scan_truncated`, and `active` |
| `read.run_result {run_id}`                                  | The Run result view, with each file's state                                                                                         |
| `read.report {run_id}`                                      | `yantra report --json`; over 512 KiB, the first part with `truncated: true` and the full `bytes`                                    |
| `read.audit {run_id, tool_calls_cursor?, captures_cursor?}` | The audit report with up to 500 tool calls and 500 captures, plus totals and cursors                                                |
| `read.artifact_window {run_id, path, from_line, limit}`     | Up to 200 lines of a JSONL file the app may show                                                                                    |
| `artifact.url {run_id, path}`                               | A signed URL for one file the app may show or download                                                                              |

`read.list` takes `limit` (1 to 200, default 50), `cursor`, `outcome` (outcome
words, plus `unknown` for runs without one), `mode`, `since`, `until`, `text`,
`workflow` and `status`. A cursor the host did not issue is refused; it never
falls back to the first page. An unknown run is a not-found error, and a file
the app may not show is refused with "That file is not an artifact the app can
open."

### Files the host keeps

All host files are under `<data-dir>/ui/`, `~/.yantra/data/ui/` by default.
They move with the data directory.

| Path                      | What it is                                                                                     |
| ------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `host.lock`               | The single-instance record: process identity, port, versions. It never holds a bare process ID |
| `host.log`, `host.log.1`  | The host's own log. It is rotated once at start when it is over 10 MiB                         |
| `host-start-failure.json` | Why the last host start failed, read by `yantra ui`                                            |
| `invocations/`            | One record per app request, plus each worker's result                                          |
| `launch/`                 | The files the host hands to workers                                                            |
| `slots.lock`              | The lock every queue change happens under                                                      |
| `chrome-profile/`         | The app window's own browser profile                                                           |

## Configuration and Permissions

- **Preferences:** `ui.theme` and `ui.surfaces`, described above. Both are
  owned by `yantra prefs`.
- **Environment:** the host captures the environment of the `yantra ui` that
  started it. Workers and drift review use that environment. To change it,
  let the host exit (it stops after 10 idle minutes) and run `yantra ui` from
  the new environment.
- **Data directory:** while the host is running, `yantra config data-dir`
  refuses to relocate. See [Configuration](configuration.md).

### Privacy and security

The host is built for a single user on a single computer.

- **Loopback only.** The host listens on `127.0.0.1`, on a port chosen at
  random, and never on `0.0.0.0`, `::` or `localhost`. It accepts a request
  only if its `Host` header is exactly `127.0.0.1:<port>`; anything else is
  refused with 421, which blocks DNS-rebinding pages.
- **Exact origin.** Every request other than GET or HEAD must carry the exact
  `Origin` `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` (403 otherwise). No CORS header is ever
  sent. A page on another local port can neither open a session nor open the
  app's socket.
- **The page talks only to the host.** A strict Content-Security-Policy limits
  the page to its own origin and the host's WebSocket. The end-to-end suite
  checks that the app makes no request beyond `127.0.0.1:<port>` and triggers
  no CSP violation.
- **Sessions.** A window must present all three of these:
  - a single-use launch code, valid for 60 seconds;
  - an `HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict` cookie;
  - a per-window capability that exists only in the page's memory, never in
    storage, the URL or a cookie.

  A cookie from one window combined with another window's capability is
  refused. A capability ends 5 minutes after its window's last connection
  closes, and 12 hours after creation in any case.

- **Never stored or logged.** The host keeps only SHA-256 digests of codes,
  cookies and capabilities, in memory. `host.log` redacts every code, cookie,
  capability, token, signed URL and secret-named field, and the security suite
  checks this with planted canary values.
- **Run files the app can fetch.** The app reaches run files only through
  typed reads and signed URLs (`/a/…`). A signed URL is bound to one window and
  lasts 5 minutes. Every signed URL stops working when its window's session
  ends or the host restarts.

  A public allowlist names every run file the app may reach. Anything it does
  not name is never served and never listed:
  - **Shown in viewers:** `brief.md`, `document.md`, `report.md`, the JSON and
    JSONL files listed under [Files and viewers](#files-and-viewers), capture
    text (`captures/cap-*.txt`), and PNG images under `screenshots/` and
    `captures/`.
  - **Read only through the Run result:** `brief.json` and `document.json`.
  - **Download only:** `brief.html` and `document.html`. HTML is never rendered
    in the app.
  - **Never served, whatever is asked:** leases, locks and mutexes, decision
    records, temporary files, sockets and browser profiles. The host lock and
    invocation records live outside run directories and are never reachable.

  The allowlist is checked when a URL is signed and again when it is fetched.
  The file's real path, after symbolic links and junctions, must stay inside
  the run directory. Each response carries the file's fixed media type and
  `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`. Every refusal is the same 404, logged by
  reason code only. See [Safety and Privacy](safety-and-privacy.md).

- **No model use in the host.** The host opens no model session. Any agentic
  work happens inside a worker, under the command's usual rules.

## Limitations

- **No exactly-once guarantee for website effects.** The host guarantees that
  each request launches a worker at most once. It cannot guarantee what a run
  did on a website before its worker died. A run that ends `owner_lost` and is
  started again is a new run, and may repeat actions. When a start's outcome is
  unknown, the host asks before starting it again rather than guessing.
- **A window cannot follow a restarted host.** After the host restarts, open a
  new window with `yantra ui`. Its session is new; runs and the queue are
  unaffected.
- **`yantra prefs set` does not reach an open window live.** Reload the window
  to apply it. Edits to `profile.yaml` apply live.
- **Browser discovery is limited** to the locations listed above. A Chrome or
  Edge installed elsewhere is not found. Use `yantra ui --print` and open the
  URL yourself.
- **The launch code is visible in the browser's process arguments**
  (`--app=<url>`). On some systems other local users can read those arguments.
  The code is single-use, lasts 60 seconds, and is spent as soon as the window
  first loads.
- **The run screens only read.** They cannot start, stop, review or resume
  runs, and there is no live screen for following a run yet. The host's queue,
  review, run following and attendance have no screens of their own in this
  release.
- **Show in folder is a command to copy.** It shows
  `yantra open <run-id> --artifact dir` instead of opening the folder.
- **`yantra list` lacks the Ledger's filters.** Its outcome, mode, date and
  text filters and cursor paging exist only in the app.
- **A source's quote is its recorded excerpt.** Yantra records one excerpt per
  source, not the exact passage behind each claim, so every claim citing a
  source shows the same quote.
- **A run without a document lists no notice text.** Its Notices region
  gives the count from run health and points to `report.md`.
- **The file list goes two levels deep.** Files deeper in a run directory are
  not listed.

For the host's process model and protocol, see
[Architecture](../architecture.md) and the
[Protocol Specification](../protocol-spec.md).
